bug_semantics: RubyLLM::Utils.underscore (and its pre-extract call sites that derived tool/agent names from class names) used the capturing regex /([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/ plus /([a-z\d])([A-Z])/. On Ruby 3.1.x the first pattern backtracks quadratically on a long run of capitals. A very long crafted class, agent, or tool name therefore causes excessive CPU in name underscoring (CWE-1333 polynomial ReDoS).
flaw_origin: cd0ca3e859d784cf0441f1872de706579d546db3 first wrote Tool.name as super.gsub(/([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/, '\1_\2').gsub(/([a-z\d])([A-Z])/, '\1_\2').downcase.delete_suffix('_tool'). Parent 2b7ff0eefcca66ec65727bfb4b49fa6dd0d20e99 used an explicit tool name string with no CamelCase-splitting regex. Later 1ba6a78 / 818b8ca2 moved and restored the same pattern; ff9c7923 copied it into Agent prompt path generation; 17a0ec4f extracted it into Utils.underscore without changing the regex. 9d75b033d7d00c4e1baa9b0afb4828faa8bd6602 replaced it with a non-backtracking lookaround UNDERSCORE_BOUNDARY and cites CVE-2026-67991. Advisory snapshot fa6f279 is a later docs commit that still contained the old regex, not the first write.

reasoning: The vulnerability is CWE-1333: the ActiveSupport-style capturing regex /([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/ backtracks quadratically on long capital runs when underscoring untrusted class/tool/agent names. The smallest first-write of that regex on a name-derivation path is cd0ca3e8, which introduced Tool.name auto-underscoring. The parent used caller-supplied names and lacked the regex, so this is not a move of an already-vulnerable helper. Later extract to Utils.underscore (17a0ec4f) and copies into Agent are the same mechanism, not a new BIC. Advisory pin fa6f279 is a post-introducer snapshot. AI is judged only from cd0ca3e8: human author/committer Carmine Paolino, no AI/bot markers, therefore NOT_AI. The lookaround rewrite in 9d75b033 is the direct fix.
